articles.title: People Are Getting Worse at Handling Uncertainty
articles.summary: Living with the unknown isn’t always easy. Not knowing if layoffs are headed your way or whether you’ll be able to afford rent would be difficult for anyone. But when the pressure of the unknown becomes so intense it interferes with daily life, this “intolerance of uncertainty,” as psychologists call it, becomes a risk factor for mental-health disorders, primarily anxiety and depression. articles.summary: I’m standing on the floor of the Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center of the California Science Center under the tail of the new exhibit of the Space Shuttle Endeavour and remembering how I felt looking up at that same shuttle on the launch pad at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. articles.title: How the War Turned Sudan Into a Country Without a Newspaper
articles.summary: A war of narratives is being waged within the war in Sudan. The warring parties—the official Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a paramilitary force—are fighting an information war through traditional and social media. Misinformation, disinformation, hate speech, and propaganda are routinely deployed, and Sudanese journalists have become targets.
